### About me
You can call me Rafik. <br>
CS Master's student at the University of Bonn, working toward a PhD somewhere down the line.My interests live at a weird and wonderful crossroads between Computational Astrophysics, Geoinformatics, and Digital Humanities. In short, I like using computers to ask big questions, whether that's about the cosmos, the planet, or the humans living on it. <br>
When I'm not studying, you'll find me diving into contemporary history, philosophy, literature, or music anywhere from classical to indie rock to folk. I write the occasional blog, love to watch documentaries, and enjoy a good debate.
Fluent in Russian and English, slowly figuring out German.

Well, feel free to reach out anytime. 
<br>


### What I'm reading now?

<p>
I'm currently reading two wonderful books. <strong>Great Expectations</strong> by Charles Dickens is a classic worth reading if you enjoy literature focused on personal development and social change, and I strongly recommend it so far. Alongside it, <strong>Barbarians to Angels</strong> by Peter S. Wells offers a fresh perspective on the so called Dark Ages after the fall of the Western Roman Empire. It is a particularly interesting read for its archaeological and historical insights, and it also includes many interesting illustrations, which I quite like. I received this book as a gift from my friend's father back in Novosibirsk, who works on Byzantine history and iconography, so it is a special recommendation from an expert in the field.
</p>
